title: Madhya Pradesh
name: Madhya Pradesh
intro: Madhya Pradesh entered the 2008 delimitation smaller than it had been for half a century. The 1976 order gave the undivided state 320 assembly seats; in November 2000 the eastern districts left to form Chhattisgarh, taking 90 of them, and the 230 that remained were used once, in 2003, before the 2008 order redrew them. The results shown here for 1980 to 1998 are the winners for the ground that later became each of these 230 seats, carried across from the undivided 320-seat list, not results from elections contested on this map.

map_caveats: The pre-2008 boundaries published here have been georectified. The source digitisation was displaced by roughly six kilometres relative to the post-2008 layer, with no scale error. The correction was fitted on the outer boundary of the state, which is unchanged between the two orders, and raises the agreement between the two outlines from an intersection-over-union of 0.91 to 0.98. Tested against the constituencies that kept their names across the redraw, none of which was used to fit it, average overlap rises from forty-two to fifty-one per cent. Readers comparing these boundaries against the source digitisation should expect them to differ, by design.

Territory lineage for this state is inferred from boundary overlap rather than from the delimitation order texts, and every seat record says so. The 1976 order for Madhya Pradesh was not available when this page was compiled, so the successor shown for each pre-2008 seat is the one holding the largest share of its area. Where the same method could be tested against order-derived lineage in other states, it agreed about four times in five.
Extent text is published for the post-2008 seats only, quoted from the 2008 order. The pre-2008 seats carry none, for the same reason.

The reservation status of the post-2008 seats is taken from the Election Commission's own records rather than from the constituency geometry, whose reservation field reports two Scheduled Caste seats and no Scheduled Tribe seats for a state that has thirty-five and forty-seven respectively.
Territory percentages are measured from the mapped boundaries in every case, and are areal shares, not shares of the electorate.

Two pre-2008 seats were tagged in the source digitisation with parliamentary constituencies in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. They have been reassigned to the Madhya Pradesh constituency whose boundary they share most.
footnotes: Madhya Pradesh was divided on 1 November 2000, when Chhattisgarh was formed from sixteen eastern districts. The 1976 order's assembly constituencies numbered 87 to 176 passed to the new state; those numbered 177 to 320 became seats 87 to 230 of the reduced Madhya Pradesh.
Reservation status reflects the category in force at the time of the relevant order, not any later reclassification.
